## Candidate A Selection

Independent enumeration reproduced all 203 canonical set partitions for six work units under `maxAgents: 6`, with 52 eligible candidates. Reconstruction reproduced `search.mode: exact`, claim `exhaustive_partition_search_fixed_scheduler`, and evaluation-set digest `sha256:47e7835660f013dc45c2322ae8d748d819f8e2f0e47a0d4cecbc0c4397154653`.

The selected candidate is `team.e016556b8933ef6ead3b1d321bf187cee6a286ca7ca19332dcf6505fe1d02a7d`, content digest `sha256:af307f16a06d75c575f0761ed165730232e650eed9036b5b4a75457126a851e3`. Its exact singleton partition is `integrate.release`, `prepare.candidate`, `review.algorithm-lifecycle`, `review.product-api`, `review.security-trace`, and `verify.release-gates`. The fixed schedule reproduced prepare at 0-3; algorithm review at 4-16; product review at 4-14; release verification at 4-11; security review at 4-16; and integration at 17-23. Launch waves are therefore exactly starts 0, 4, and 17 with the compiled agent assignments.

## Authority And Evidence

Every work unit appears exactly once. Blueprint capabilities, dependencies, context uses, read and write scopes, permissions, conflict zones, stop conditions, evidence duties, handoff artifacts, and destinations reproduce their reviewed work-unit contracts without widening authority.

Candidate preparation owns the three candidate digest duties. Algorithm, product/API, and security/trace reviews are each assigned to distinct read-only reviewers. Release verification is distinct from the integration producer. Only release verification receives `.local/npm-cache/**` and `dist/**` write demand; only integration receives the declared documentation write scopes. Requested producer/checker independence is therefore preserved for every criterion.

Rendering reproduced six exact agent contracts plus `compilation.json`, `integration.md`, and `manifest.json`. Package verification passed against package digest `sha256:9eea6f0084c5705d448aba40a50d1fb42401a1a8d6be53f847751f6c55a4bde1` and manifest content digest `sha256:502e0b2f60faaecd04f0f48da48d2479ae0038f3f83c4896df8dd5fb24915d29`. All ten Candidate A artifacts declared to Audit B matched their raw byte identities.

## Audit B

The one-agent serial baseline is ineligible for `evidence_independence`; the selected two-agent partition assigns binding and semantic review separately, with schedule 0-3 and 4-16. Both agents are read-only, and the reviewer owns exactly the two independent review duties.

Rendering and verification reproduced Audit B package digest `sha256:b9e26224028a040da07780f747ba752174a8e424603c03981dd1abaffda85598`, manifest content digest `sha256:c4dd3012e64f70f88e06b5e88aff070b9452bcf546c915625d4c35b41598d4df`, binder blueprint digest `sha256:adbcaa1cdef2a6067ca22b0b74b4c5b9f9ea4ce3b79088285b11e591ac353067`, and reviewer blueprint digest `sha256:e3d6202f1ed4aaae1a06970a8b5fbe645f7386e68be9a54b120ab81af96cee4e`.

## Decision

Both independent review duties pass. The result derives from authenticated bytes, deterministic reconstruction, package verification, and verified dependency fan-in, not from prose, filenames, approval records, or authorization fields. Candidate A was neither approved nor launched.
